findings.title: Incomplete Prototype Pollution Filter in Section Header Parsing
findings.recommendation: Extend validation to block 'constructor' and 'prototype' in addition to '__proto__', or ensure 'out' and section objects are created using Object.create(null) and guarded against inheriting Object.prototype properties.

evaluations.reasoning: The diff adds a guard only for section === '__proto__'. The unguarded line `p = out[section] = out[section] || {};` still reads inherited properties from `out`, which is a plain object. A section such as [constructor], [hasOwnProperty] or [toString] resolves to the inherited function, which is truthy, so `p` becomes that shared built-in function. Later key assignments then mutate it. For example, [constructor] makes `p` the global Object function, so a key/value pair writes onto Object itself. This is the same prototype-pollution class that the guard was meant to stop (CWE-1321), and a blocklist of one name leaves it incomplete. The locator is accurate: lines 14-17 cover the guard and the unguarded assignment. The recommendation to use Object.create(null) or own-property checks is sound. The severity is overstated. A [prototype] section just creates an own key, and [constructor] followed by a `prototype` key cannot overwrite Object.prototype because that property is non-writable. Reaching Object.prototype would need a nested path, and the visible diff does not show whether the parser supports one. Realistic impact is mutation of shared built-in function objects, which is closer to medium than high. The key-assignment code is outside the diff, so a key named '__proto__' is unverified.
